title: SRE After-Action Framework and On-call Mentoring Guide
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This document defines a repeatable After-Action Review (AAR) process tailored to Redwood Inference incident lifecycles, and pairs it with a practical on-call mentoring and succession program. It is intended for SREs, on-call engineers, support leads, and engineering managers who participate in incident response, runbook maintenance, and readiness drills.

Goals
- Produce concise, action-oriented post-incident artifacts that reduce repeat incidents.
- Shorten mean time to recovery by improving knowledge transfer across rotations.
- Grow on-call confidence through structured shadowing, feedback, and remediation coaching.

Scope
- Applies to production incidents (Sev1–Sev3) and to any multi-team incident escalations.
- Includes runbook updates, postmortem/AAR, incident communication templates, and game day design.
- Does NOT replace legal/security-required incident handling for data breaches (see security incident procedures).

1) Incident lifecycle and AAR timeline

Summary timeline (targeted SLAs)
1. Detection & triage (T0–T10m): Pager fired; initial ack within 5 minutes.
2. Stabilization & mitigation (T10m–T2h): Contain blast radius; apply short-term mitigation.
3. Recovery & verification (T2h–T24h): Restore service and validate correctness.
4. Post-incident AAR kickoff (T+24–72h): IC schedules AAR, invites stakeholders.
5. Postmortem published (T+7 days target): Draft circulated; action items created.

Roles & responsibilities
- Incident Commander (IC): Drives triage and timelines.
- Communications Lead: Publishes status page and customer updates.
- Tech Lead / Owner: Implements fixes, verifies root cause.
- Scribe: Captures timeline and decisions in shared doc.
- Mentoring Buddy: Assigned mentor for the on-call engineer handling the incident (see section 3).

Severity classification (summary)
| Severity | Definition | Detection/Impact threshold | Response window |
|---------|----------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------|------------------|
| Sev1 | System-wide outage or data loss affecting >25% customers | Major SLO breaches (>99.9th pct tokens error) | Immediate (timer start T0) |
| Sev2 | Partial outage or major degradation for subset of customers | Latency/throughput degradation causing elevated error rates | Acknowledge within 10m |
| Sev3 | Service degradation with low customer impact or single-customer issues | Isolated errors, non-critical regressions | Acknowledge within 1 hour |

2) Containment & runbook update pattern

Containment checklist (first responders)
- Confirm scope (services, regions, customer impact).
- Switch traffic to fallback model/region if configured.
- Disable automated rollouts (if active).
- Apply rate-limiting mitigation keys or throttles.
- Capture relevant logs and full KV cache markers; preserve for analysis.

Runbook update rules (post-incident)
1. The engineer who executed any manual mitigation must add a section to the runbook within 48 hours explaining steps and rationale.
2. Runbook edits require a short review by the owning team and the SRE mentor.
3. If an ad-hoc mitigation becomes recurring, convert to a permanent operational step and add a rollback path.

Example quick mitigation snippet
```
# Example: drain a problematic node and restart replica
kubectl cordon gpu-pool-node-42
kubectl drain gpu-pool-node-42 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl rollout restart statefulset/model-inference-pool
```

3) On-call mentoring and succession program

Objective: Turn incident experience into organized learning and reduce tribal knowledge risk.

Program components
- Shadow Week (first rotation): New on-call engineers shadow a senior mentor for at least three incidents or for five shift-hours.
- Mentoring Buddy: Every on-call has an assigned buddy for the rotation who reviews post-incident notes and provides feedback within 72 hours.
- Rotation Succession Plan: Engineers must nominate a successor two weeks before planned PTO; manager confirms coverage.
- Knowledge Artifacts: Each incident must produce a one-paragraph learning note ("what I learned") added to the team wiki within 7 days.

Mentor checklist (for each incident)
1. Review the timeline and key decisions.
2. Provide 30–60 minute synchronous review if the incident was Sev1/Sev2.
3. Suggest two runbook edits or test cases to reduce recurrence.
4. Sign off on runbook changes as reviewer.

4) AAR / postmortem template (required fields)
- Title: [Service] — [Short summary of impact]
- Incident date/time: Start / End (UTC)
- Severity: Sev1|Sev2|Sev3
- Summary (2–4 sentences): What happened, customer impact, current state.
- Timeline: Ordered events with timestamps and actor names.
- Root cause analysis: Summary and evidence.
- Detection & tooling gaps: Why pager fired and where detection failed (if applicable).
- Mitigations & recovery steps: Short-term actions taken and owners.
- Long-term corrective actions: Action items with owner and due date.
- Learnings & impact on runbooks: What to change in runbooks, dashboards, or alerts.
- Postmortem review notes: Feedback from reviewers and final sign-off.

Action item format (table inserted into the postmortem)
| Action ID | Owner | Description | Due date | Status |
| A-2025-001 | Jane Doe | Add synthetic test for KV cache expiry | 2025-04-15 | open |

Delivery expectations
- Draft circulated to reviewers within 5 business days.
- Finalized and published on the incident tracker within 7 business days.
- All action items tracked in the team’s task board; overdue items escalated during retro.
content_continued:
5) Game days and simulation curriculum

Design principles
- Simulate real traffic shapes and alert triggers rather than toy faults.
- Rotate roles (IC, comms lead, tech lead, scribe) so everyone practices different responsibilities.
- Include a post-exercise AAR with the same template as a production incident.

Quarterly game day template
- Pre-brief (30m): Objectives and environment snapshot.
- Scenario run (90m): Inject failure, allow teams to discover and mitigate.
- Recovery verification (30m): Validate service and customer-facing checks.
- AAR (60m): Capture learning notes, update runbooks.

Sample scenarios
- Model-serving KV cache corruption under burst load.
- Cross-region failover with stale routing rules.
- Canary rollout causing 20% error rate on a critical endpoint.

6) Status page and customer communications (templates)

Initial acknowledgement (use in first 15 minutes)
Subject: [Redwood] Incident detected: [service] — Investigating
Body:
We are investigating an issue affecting [service]. Customers may experience [symptoms]. We will provide an update within 30 minutes or sooner. Impacted regions: [us-west-2, eu-central].

Hourly update (use when active)
Subject: [Redwood] Update: [service] incident — [ETA or progress summary]
Body:
Current status: [mitigations in progress / traffic rerouted / partial recovery]
What we are doing: [short bullets]
Next update: [time or condition]

Resolved message (use when fully recovered)
Subject: [Redwood] Resolved: [service] incident
Body:
Summary of impact: [what happened, who was affected]
Root cause: [short phrase]
Customer guidance: [any user actions required or none]
Link to postmortem: [link]

Status page policy
- The Communications Lead must publish an initial status page entry within 30 minutes of incident escalation.
- Updates should be posted at least hourly until recovery or when materially new info is available.
- Resolved entries must include a link to the AAR within 7 business days.

7) Post-incident closure and metrics

Closure checklist
- Verify all actions in postmortem have owners and due dates.
- Confirm runbook edits merged and reviewed.
- Mark incident as closed in the incident tracker only after corrective tests pass in staging.

Key metrics to track per incident
- MTTR (time to first mitigation, time to full recovery)
- Number of on-call handoffs during the incident
- Number of runbook edits created from the incident
- Recurrence rate (repeat incidents with same RCA within 90 days)

8) Governance & ownership

- Each service must have a designated runbook owner and an SRE mentor assigned quarterly.
- The on-call rotation manager (engineering operations) is responsible for scheduling shadow weeks and confirming successors for PTO.
- The incident review board meets monthly to triage overdue action items and evaluate systemic trends.

Related references
- Incident command playbook and escalation matrix (link)
- On-call simulation cookbook and rotation guidelines (link)
- Security breach handling procedures (link to security-and-compliance)

Appendix: Quick checklist for a new on-call engineer
- Read the team runbook and open the latest 3 AARs for your service.
- Complete one shadow shift with your mentoring buddy.
- Verify ICS access: pager, status page, runbook editor, incident tracker.
- Run the local recovery smoke test (script path: ops/scripts/smoke-recover.sh).
